_note: Copy to settings.json (gitignored) and fill in. The FIRST instance is the in-memory fake adapter: it loads and polls as copied, with no credentials — QUICKSTART step 5 runs against it. Later instances need their env-var references exported first: values of the form 'env:NAME' under auth are read from the environment at runtime — never put literal credentials in any settings file. Delete any instance you are not using; every instance kept must name a shipped adapter and resolve its env references, or the engine refuses to start. Every channel starts at reply_policy 'never' on purpose: watch first, promote later (docs/QUICKSTART.md step 4). Every key in this file is READ by the engine; a key it does not read is refused at load (a key that configures nothing would let you believe you changed behaviour when nothing changed). Keys starting with '_' are comments.

_reply_policies_doc.never: read-only; core/outbox refuses send() for this target
_reply_policies_doc.staged: drafts written to state/outbox/, explicit operator gate required before send
_reply_policies_doc.direct: adapter may send with no click, after outbox audit logging — only through an adapter that declares direct sends on; the slack adapter declares them OFF, so a direct policy on it is refused at outbox construction and again at the send seam

_send_keys_doc.instances[].send_marker: optional prefix (e.g. "[AGENT]") every send from the connection must carry: prepended when a draft is staged on the write surface, required again at the click
_send_keys_doc.instances[].answerers: optional list of sender ids whose replies may close OTHER people's asks (the agent's bot user, the operators); an ask posed by a listed answerer is closed by the other party; omitted, any non-asker's answer closes an ask
_send_keys_doc.instances[].channels[].kind: optional 'dm' or 'channel': a 1:1 direct message is answered top-level and closed by the DM rule; omitted, a Slack-shaped D... id infers dm and any other id is a channel
